lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Healthy body, happy mind! Today, we follow the rainbow from the Village of Springs. We climb up, up, up, above the clouds. Look! The rainbow is a huge bridge! But its colors are very pale. An old white crane flies down to meet us. Her name is Iris. She is the keeper of the bridge. She says, Welcome to the Rainbow Bridge! This bridge connects many countries. Say it with me. This bridge connects many countries. Wonderful! Kiko asks, Why are the colors so pale? Iris answers, Not many friends visit now. Let's read the sign at the bridge gate. "Welcome to the Rainbow Bridge! This bridge connects many countries. Please walk to Friendship Plaza in the middle. Meet new friends and share your stories. Every kind word brings back one color. When all seven colors shine, the bridge will be happy again. From Iris, Keeper of the Bridge." Where is Friendship Plaza? In the middle of the bridge. How many colors are there? Seven. Now, phonics. Today, we listen to words we use in Japanese, too. But English sounds different! Energy. EN-er-gy. Not e-ne-ru-gi. Allergy. AL-ler-gy. Vitamin. VI-ta-min. Hamburger. HAM-bur-ger. Say the strong part loudly. Let's walk to Friendship Plaza!

Aino is from Finland. She says, Moi! Amara is from Kenya. She says, Jambo! Mateo is from Mexico. He says, Hola! Birimo is our interpreter. Moi, Jambo, Hola! That means hello, hello, hello! Before we sit down on the soft carpet, Haru takes off his shoes. He says, In Japan, we take off our shoes at home. Say it with me. In Japan, we take off our shoes at home. Great! Aino smiles. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, What do children in your country do for fun? Today, we are writing an introduction of Japan for the World Question Box. Riko starts with a big fact. Japan has four seasons. Say it with me. Japan has four seasons. Wonderful! Then she writes about her town. In my town, there is a big festival in summer. A good introduction has a beginning, some facts, and an ending. Let's read Riko's draft. "My Japan. Japan has four seasons. In spring, you can see cherry blossoms. In summer, we watch fireworks. In autumn, the leaves turn red and yellow. In winter, it snows in many places. In my town, there is a big festival in summer. People in Japan say itadakimasu before meals. It means thank you for the food. Please visit Japan someday!" What can you see in spring? Cherry blossoms. What does itadakimasu mean? Thank you for the food. Count the sentences. There are nine. Perfect! Now, phonics. Hamburger. HAM-bur-ger. Judo. A Japanese word in English. We eat lunch at school. At is small and quick. Made of. Made-of, the words hold hands. Unhappiness. Un plus happy, change the y to i, plus ness. Japan is a wonderful place to introduce!

phonics.tipJa: ワールド28 の まとめ: volunteer は vol-un-TEER と さいごを つよく。karaoke は 英語でも つかう 日本語。summer and winter の and は よわく。keep in touch は「キーピンタッチ」。un＋kind＋ness で unkindness、friendly＋ness で friendliness（y を i に）。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Mochi is a kind of rice cake. I think you'll love it because it's soft and sweet. Today is the grand finale on the Rainbow Bridge. All our friends stand together. Aino says Moi, Amara says Jambo, and Mateo says Hola. They are different words, but they all mean hello. Haru says, Our languages are different, but our hearts are the same. Say it with me. Our languages are different, but our hearts are the same. Fantastic! Suddenly, the last color comes back. Violet! Now the bridge shines in all seven colors. Iris gives us a special badge. Let's read it. "Rainbow Bridge Friendship Badge. This badge is for Haru, Riko, Kiko, and Birimo. You explained Japan, shared your opinions, and listened to new friends. You made the bridge shine again. Congratulations! You finished Stage 3. Keep in touch with your friends, and keep your hearts open. From Iris" What color came back last? Violet. What did they finish? Stage 3. We say, Thank you, Iris! Thank you, everyone! Then we look at the light far away. Next stop, the Lighthouse of Ideas! Now, phonics. Volunteer. vol-un-TEER. Karaoke. A Japanese word in English. I like summer and winter. And is small and quick. Keep in touch. Keep-in-touch. Unkindness. Un plus kind plus ness. Friendliness. Friendly, change the y to i, plus ness. See you at the lighthouse!
